# Chung-Won Woo (우청원) — Carbon, ESG & Innovation Accounting Research

> Associate Professor of Accounting, Changwon National University, South Korea.
> Empirical research on how carbon regulation (EU CBAM), climate risk, ESG,
> innovation strategy, and information-security investment show up in firms'
> costs, disclosures, audits, and market value. 39+ peer-reviewed publications,
> 1,450+ citations, h-index 17. Formerly Research Fellow at the Science and
> Technology Policy Institute (STEPI), Korea's national think tank for S&T policy.

## Key papers (plain-language summary pages with FAQ)

- [EU CBAM and Korean listed firms (2024)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/cbam-korea-2024.html): First event study of the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism's impact on Korean firm value — carbon-intensive firms suffered significant negative returns, priced in over the medium to long term. Review of Accounting and Policy Studies 29(4).
- [Climate change exposure and corporate performance (2024)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/climate-exposure-2024.html): Firm-level climate exposure erodes financial and energy performance; CEOs' green experience mitigates the damage. Journal of Cleaner Production 461, 142653.
- [Innovation and asymmetric cost behavior (2022)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/innovation-cost-stickiness-2022.html): Innovating firms show greater cost stickiness — managers deliberately retain slack resources to protect innovation when sales fall. Korean Accounting Review 47(3).
- [R&D strategy and cost stickiness (2021)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/rd-strategy-cost-stickiness-2021.html): R&D-intensive firms hoard resources in downturns; capitalized vs. expensed R&D produce different cost asymmetry. Technology Analysis & Strategic Management 33(9).
- [Openness, appropriability, and innovation performance (2023)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/openness-innovation-appropriability-2023.html): Collaboration breadth/depth and geographic proximity affect product vs. process innovation differently. Technology Analysis & Strategic Management 35(1).
- [Predicting ICT innovation with machine learning (2024)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/ict-innovation-machine-learning-2024.html): Random forest predicts ICT business-process innovation; external information sources are the most critical driver. Technology Analysis & Strategic Management 36(9).
- [Social enterprise sustainability through innovation (2025)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/social-enterprise-sustainability-2025.html): Technology orientation builds the capability that drives social enterprises' financial performance; monetary incentives boost financial, not social, outcomes. Sustainable Development 33.
- [Carbon risk, audit hours and audit fees (2023)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/carbon-risk-audit-fees-2023.html): Korean firms with higher carbon intensity receive significantly more audit hours, but carbon risk is not priced into audit fees. Korea International Accounting Review 110, 181-215.
- [Suppliers' COGS ratio and environmental activities (2024)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/supplier-cogs-environmental-2024.html): A 10 percentage point higher cost-of-goods-sold ratio cuts a supplier's likelihood of environmental activity by about 24.6% — but business-group affiliation reverses the relationship. Review of Accounting and Policy Studies 29(4), 215-234.
- [IT and information security investment and firm value (2026)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/it-security-investment-firm-value-2026.html): Inverted-U between IT investment and firm value with a turning point near 11.66% of total assets; dedicated CISO and CPO roles mitigate over-investment inefficiency. Review of Accounting and Policy Studies 31(2), 123-149.
- [IT investment and cost efficiency (2025)](https://woocw3.github.io/papers/it-investment-cost-efficiency-2025.html): DEA evidence that information-security-disclosing firms are more cost efficient and that IT investment plus dedicated IT personnel raise technical efficiency. Korean Business Education Review 40(2), 129-149.
